resolutions.researcher_notes: Status is inferred, not stated verbatim as 'operating'. OPEC ASB 2012 (opec.org/.../ASB2012.pdf, live link dead/redirects to homepage per known gotcha; recovered via Wayback snapshot 20250110032615, a genuine 7.8MB PDF) Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' p.75 lists 'Intesar/Brega — Zueitina — 207 [mi] — 42 [in] — 42,480,884 [1,000 scm/yr]' among rated, in-service lines as of year-end 2011 (extracted via pdftotext -f 77 -l 77 on the recovered PDF; url_verifier can't see through the zip-deflate-encoded PDF text stream so its substring check reports 200-only, confirmed manually). Zueitina Oil Co's own projects page (operator's site, Wayback snapshot from Dec 2023, still live) describes the same 42-inch, Intisar-103A-to-Brega gas line as company transport infrastructure ('project 85% complete' as of the ~2010 write-up); its continued presence on the live corporate site 13+ years later plus OPEC's 2011 capacity listing together support 'operating' by context. No source states a shutdown/decommission.

OPEC ASB 2012 (Wayback-recovered PDF) lists this line in Table 4.10 titled 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' — direct categorical confirmation. Zueitina's own project page is titled 'مشروع نقل غاز حقل الإنتصار 103 أ إلى الشبكة الساحلية' ('Gas transfer project from Intisar field 103A to the coastal network') and repeatedly describes natural gas ('الغاز الطبيعي') volumes in million standard cubic feet/day. Two independent sources, both explicit.

Zueitina's project page states pipe-laying, engineering, topographic/geotechnical survey work was underway and phase-1 (pipeline) construction had reached 85% completion ('بلغت نسبة الإنجاز الكلية للمشروع %85'), and references a joint NOC/Zueitina project briefing held 'يوم الأحد 7/2/2010م' (Sunday, 7 Feb 2010) — i.e. the article itself dates to 2010 with construction well underway/nearing completion that year, supporting ConstructionYear=2010. OPEC ASB 2012 (reporting year-end 2011 data) already lists the line with a rated capacity, consistent with the pipeline having been substantially completed by/around 2010-2011. No source gives an exact 'construction start' date distinct from this — treated as best-available support, not a certainty; ConstructionMonth is not stated in the brief so not addressed.

OPEC ASB 2012, Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', p.75: row 'Intesar/Brega — Zueitina — 207[mi] — 42[in] — 42,480,884[1,000 scm/yr]' = 42,480,884,000 scm/yr = 42.48 bcm/yr — EXACT match to the brief's 42.48 bcm/y. Live opec.org link is dead (redirects to homepage per the known gotcha); recovered via Wayback (20250110032615), a genuine 7.8MB PDF confirmed with pdftotext. Only one independent source found for this exact figure (single-sourced to OPEC). FLAG: Zueitina's own project page describes the *fully built-out, multi-phase* coastal-network gas supply target as ~1,500 million standard cf/day (~15.5 bcm/yr equivalent) — a materially different, lower number than the pipeline's 42.48 bcm/yr OPEC-rated capacity. These likely describe different things (single-pipe rated/design capacity vs. planned aggregate delivered volumes to the coastal grid after compression), but the discrepancy is large enough that it's worth a second look before treating 42.48 as fully reconciled.

CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (p.75) lists this line's length as '207' under a column explicitly headed 'Length (miles)'. 207 miles = 333.13 km, which matches the brief's LengthKnown=333.00 km almost exactly (i.e. the mainsheet value looks like a straight mi->km conversion of OPEC's '207'). HOWEVER Zueitina Oil Co's own project page (the pipeline's operator, an independent and arguably more authoritative primary source for its own asset) states the pipeline's length directly as 'بطول 207 كيلو متر تقريباً' — i.e. 207 KILOMETERS, not miles. So the two primary sources use the same raw number '207' but in different units, and only one of them can be right: either the pipeline is ~207 km (per the operator) or ~333 km (per OPEC-as-miles). Given the operator built and runs the line, 207 km is plausibly the more trustworthy figure, and 333 km may be an artifact of a mi/km mixup somewhere upstream. Citing OPEC (Wayback) here only because it is the source that numerically supports the brief's stated 333.00 km value — but this should be reconciled against Zueitina's 207 km statement, ideally by adjusting the mainsheet rather than accepting this ref at face value. Tier kept low given the direct conflict.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 lists Diameter=42 (inches) for this exact line. Zueitina's project page independently states 'أنبوب قطره 42 بوصة' ('a pipe 42 inches in diameter'). Two independent sources, exact numeric match, no ambiguity.

Zueitina's project page states the pipe runs 'من حقل 103أ إلى البريقة على الساحل' ('from field 103A to Brega on the coast'), and Zueitina's own about-us history page lists field 103A under 'حقول الانتصار (المشاركة) النفطية' — i.e. field 103A IS the Intisar field, confirming StartLocation='Intesar Oil field'. OPEC ASB Table 4.10 independently lists the same line as 'Intesar/Brega'. Both Intisar field (Sirte Basin oil/gas concession area) and Mersa Brega (an established Libyan coastal town/oil terminal in the Al Wahat area) are well-established Libyan place names consistent with StartState/Province='Sirte Basin' and EndState/Province='Al Wahat'; no source contradicts the province/governorate attributions.

OPEC ASB Table 4.10 lists 'Owner or operator' = 'Zueitina' for this line. The project page is itself hosted on زueitina.com.ly and describes the project as one Zueitina was entrusted with by NOC ('عهدت المؤسسة الوطنية للنفط لشركة الزويتينة للنفط للمتابعة والإشراف عليه' — 'NOC entrusted Zueitina Oil Co. with following up and supervising it'), i.e. self-attributed operatorship. OperatorLocalLanguage 'شركة الزويتينة للنفط' matches the company's own Arabic name as it appears verbatim on its site.

Zueitina's own 'About Us' history page (Arabic version, Wayback 2011, and the current English version, Wayback 2026 — same content, 15 years apart) states verbatim: for its 'Muqasama' (production-sharing) fields, ownership is '81% المؤسسة الوطنية للنفط [NOC] — 14.25% أوكسيدنتال [Occidental] — 4.75% أو.ام.في [OMV]' — an EXACT match to the brief's Owner1/2/3 values and percentages. Both language mirrors are the same company/source, so independence is false (1 source, corroborated across two snapshots in time rather than across two organizations). CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: the SAME about-us page lists field '103أ' (Intisar/103A — i.e. the very field this pipeline originates from) under the heading 'حقول الانتصار (المشاركة) النفطية' — the 'Musharaka' (participation) field category — whose ownership split is stated elsewhere on the same page as 51% NOC / 36.75% Occidental / 12.25% OMV, NOT the 81/14.25/4.75 'Muqasama' split the brief lists. So while 81/14.25/4.75 is a real, exact, sourced Zueitina ownership split, it may be the wrong category for this specific field/pipeline — the correct split per the same source could instead be 51/36.75/12.25. Flagging for review rather than silently 'fixing' the mainsheet; tier kept at medium given the source is strong but the category match is in question.
